title: What Generation Ships Is
definition: Generation Ships: city-sized starships carrying whole generations to the stars.
description:
Generation Ships: city-sized starships carrying whole generations to the stars. This is Interstellar & Deep Space Futures at its most ambitious — life-support research, fusion propulsion engineering and closed ecology operations converging on a single goal: making generation hull real.

Why it matters: Interstellar & Deep Space Futures will decide spin gravity outcomes this century. Generation Ships is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working generation hull, the larger life-support vision stalls, and with it, the fusion propulsion systems that depend on it.

This database documents Generation Ships in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Generation Ships
definition: Today's documented research behind Generation Ships.
description:
The road to Generation Ships is already being paved. The Voyager probes, launched in 1977, are the only human objects in interstellar space. The 100 Year Starship project (DARPA/NASA seeded) studies the capabilities needed for interstellar flight within a century.

NASA's Kilopower/KRUSTY project demonstrated compact fission power for deep-space outposts. Together these programs form the life-support foundation that Generation Ships will build on — the fusion propulsion results, the closed ecology methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as fusion propulsion research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: The generation hull
definition: The generation hull: a load-bearing component of Generation Ships.
description:
The pressure hull and structure that carries everything: radiation shielding, micrometeorite armor, and spin-gravity sections built around the life-support core.

In the Generation Ships architecture, the generation hull is load-bearing: without it the generation hull fails outright — Generation Ships stops being Generation Ships at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Generation Ships-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2032 — First long-duration spin gravity testbed runs a sealed generatio
title: 2032 — First long-duration spin gravity testbed runs a sealed generatio
definition: 2032 milestone on the Generation Ships roadmap.
description:
First long-duration spin gravity testbed runs a sealed generation hull habitat for 1,000 days on Earth, proving the life-support recycling math.

What must be true first: the life-support results have to replicate outside the lab, fusion propulsion manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and closed ecology operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed life-support demonstrations, fusion propulsion cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting closed ecology uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Generation Ships
definition: Estimates Generation Ships readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Generation Ships components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a generation hull that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Generation Ships Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Generation Ships operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Generation Ships installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 5978 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where life-support monitoring, fusion propulsion redundancy, or closed ecology maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Generation Ships Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Generation Ships: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Generation Ships — city-sized starships carrying whole generations to the stars.

Phase 1 — Prove (life-support): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (fusion propulsion): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (closed ecology): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (spin gravity): generation hull as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and deep-space-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
